definitions.explanation: The incoming tide, and the high water it brings. The everyday native word; the technical term for high tide is {満潮|まんちょう}.

examples.english: The waves are high at high tide.

examples.japanese: {満|み}ち{潮|しお}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{岩場|いわば}→岩場：27478_iwaba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{沈|しず}んで→沈む：02061_shizumu⟧しまう。
examples.english: At high tide, these rocks become submerged in the sea.

notes:
{満|み}ち{潮|しお} comes from ⟦{満|み}ちる→満ちる：02428_michiru⟧ (to fill, to rise) and ⟦{潮|しお}→潮：13369_shio⟧ (tide). It names the tide while it is coming in as well as the high water itself. The Sino-Japanese ⟦{満潮|まんちょう}→満潮：06530_manchou⟧ is the term used in tide tables and news; it means high tide, the moment the water is highest. The opposite of {満|み}ち{潮|しお} is ⟦{引|ひ}き{潮|しお}→引き潮：07148_hikishio⟧.

WATCH OUT:
The kanji 満潮 on its own is normally read まんちょう; みちしお is written with okurigana, {満|み}ち{潮|しお}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {満|み}ち{潮|しお}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: the tide comes in
- {満|み}ち{潮|しお}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時|とき}: at high tide (in tide tables, {満潮時|まんちょうじ})

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{引|ひ}き{潮|しお}→引き潮：07148_hikishio⟧: low tide — the opposite, native reading
- ⟦{満潮|まんちょう}→満潮：06530_manchou⟧: high tide — the technical term, used in tide tables and forecasts
